questions.title: Modules practice 1
questions.prompt: Which syntax imports a named export called `add`?
choices: import { add } from "./math.js";
import add with "./math.js";
include add from "./math.js";
require { add } "./math.js";
questions.explanation: Named imports use braces around the exact exported name and a from clause containing the module path.

questions.title: Modules practice 2
questions.prompt: How often is a module normally evaluated when imported by several files?
choices: Once, then its exports are reused
Once per function call
Twice for named exports
It is never evaluated
questions.explanation: The module system evaluates one module instance and shares its exported bindings with the files that import it.

questions.title: Trace Modules
questions.prompt: What output does this code produce? Enter each line in order.
questions.explanation: The exporting file defines one reusable operation, and the importing file names the same exported binding. The resulting output is '12'.

questions.title: Modules practice 5
questions.prompt: `math.js` has `export function double(...)`. Which import matches it?
choices: import { double } from "./math.js"; — braces, because it is a named export
import double from "./math.js"; — no braces
import * double from "./math.js";
require("./math.js").double;
questions.explanation: A named export is imported with braces around the exact name: `import { double }`. The brace-free form is only for a `default` export, so it would import `undefined` here. `import * double` is invalid syntax, and `require` is CommonJS, not ES-module syntax.

questions.title: Modules concept check 1
questions.prompt: Why can a JavaScript import fail even when the exported name is correct?
choices: A correct export can still fail to load when its path is wrong. Relative browser imports normally include the file extension, and a server must deliver the module with an appropriate JavaScript content type.
Export everything in the file whether callers need it or not.
Mix named and default import styles incorrectly.
Use a path that does not match where the module lives.
questions.explanation: A correct export can still fail to load when its path is wrong. Relative browser imports normally include the file extension, and a server must deliver the module with an appropriate JavaScript content type. This matters because module code depends on what a file exports, what another file imports, and when the imported value runs.

questions.title: Modules concept check 2
questions.prompt: Which choice describes a reliable Modules practice?
choices: Depend on hidden side effects when importing.
Give each module one clear responsibility.
Put several unrelated responsibilities in one module.
Forget the file extension where the runtime expects it.
questions.explanation: Give each module one clear responsibility. This matters because module code depends on what a file exports, what another file imports, and when the imported value runs.

questions.title: Modules concept check 3
questions.prompt: Which Modules code review note is accurate?
choices: Create circular imports for ordinary helper functions.
Duplicate helpers instead of importing them.
Export only values other files need.
Rename an export without updating import sites.
questions.explanation: Export only values other files need. This matters because module code depends on what a file exports, what another file imports, and when the imported value runs.

questions.title: Modules concept check 4
questions.prompt: Which Modules habit prevents a common mistake?
choices: Use modules to hide unclear ownership.
Run app startup code just by importing a helper.
Import from an index file without checking what it re-exports.
Match named and default import styles.
questions.explanation: Match named and default import styles. This matters because module code depends on what a file exports, what another file imports, and when the imported value runs.

questions.title: Modules concept check 5
choices: Check relative paths and file extensions.
Use relative paths that break when files move.
Expose internal constants as public API.
Avoid modules and keep all code in one file.
questions.explanation: Check relative paths and file extensions. This matters because module code depends on what a file exports, what another file imports, and when the imported value runs.

questions.title: Modules concept check 6
questions.prompt: Which statement is accurate about Modules?
choices: Make modules depend on browser globals for pure logic.
Split a program into files with explicit exports and imports.
Assume bundlers and browsers resolve paths identically.
Import a value only for its name, not its behavior.
questions.explanation: Split a program into files with explicit exports and imports. This matters because module code depends on what a file exports, what another file imports, and when the imported value runs.
